measurement: batch=256 per seed, seeds 0-4, CPU; fraction_clamped is over the (B,N) tensor
what_this_is: Per-backend record of whether the anatomy prior actually reached each backend. A 0% clamp rate means one of two very different things and this table separates them: timescale_applied=true with 0% means the prior fitted inside the backend's calibrated support; timescale_applied=false means the prior never arrived and the backend's regional values are its defaults.

stuart_landau.reason: Stuart-Landau exposes no relaxation-time parameter the prior can modulate. 'a' is the Hopf bifurcation parameter and changes sign, so a multiplicative timescale modulation would move parcels across the bifurcation rather than rescale their dynamics; 'f' is an oscillation frequency, not an autocorrelation decay rate. Mapping either would be a different scientific claim, not a unit conversion.
stuart_landau.ei_reason: Hopf normal form has no separate inhibitory population, so no parameter means 'inhibitory gain'.

jansen_rit.ei_reason: Jansen-Rit has no scalar inhibitory-gain parameter. The candidate is B (inhibitory PSP amplitude, mV), deliberately not mapped: B co-determines the alpha peak with A and the C-ratios, so scaling it alone would confound an E/I change with a spectral one, and the receptor-derived E/I contrast is route-fragile in per-parcel sign.

linear_gaussian.ei_reason: Linear-Gaussian reference has one population per region and no separate inhibitory state, so no parameter means 'inhibitory gain'.

kuramoto.reason: Kuramoto is phase-only: it has no amplitude and therefore no relaxation timescale to modulate. Its single time parameter 'f' is an oscillation frequency, not an autocorrelation decay rate.
kuramoto.ei_reason: Phase-only model with no separate inhibitory population.
